subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage: Teacher's note, Bhavna, nursery class. During outdoor water play, Minakshi began to shake, arms wrapped round herself, teeth chattering. I could not tell whether she was cold, since the wind had picked up, or excited about the sprinkler game, or just tired. I wrapped her in a dry towel, sat with her and asked how her body felt. “Jumpy,” she said. The shaking eased after a while with the towel and some warm water. I told her mother at pickup and suggested asking the doctor if it keeps happening.

qa.q: What did Bhavna wrap around Minakshi?
qa.a: She wrapped a dry towel around Minakshi.

qa.q: What might Minakshi have been feeling when she said “jumpy”, and what else could explain the shaking?
qa.a: Possibly excitement about the sprinkler game she had waited for, though the wind making her cold or tiredness could also cause it. Her one word does not settle which.

qa.q: What did Bhavna do that suited most of the possible causes, and what should happen if it keeps happening?
qa.a: The dry towel, warm water and calm company help with cold, nerves and tiredness alike. If the shaking keeps happening, checking with the doctor is sensible, as she told the mother.

qa.q: How might Minakshi's mother feel reading about the shaking?
qa.a: She may feel reassured by the calm care but also watchful, since she has been asked to notice if it repeats. What she knows about Minakshi may help work out the cause.

grounding: Trembling in a young child can come from cold, excitement or tiredness; warmth helps and a persistent tremor goes to the doctor.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage: Evening at the temple fair, the wooden swing-wheel creaked round. Sudha, five, stood with her hand in her grandfather Tanvir's, her whole body trembling, knees, fingers, even her chin. The breeze off the river had turned cold and her shawl hung off one shoulder. “Are you scared?” Tanvir asked. She shook her head, then nodded, then said, “I want to go.” He wrapped the shawl round her, crouched to her height and said they could watch one round first. She kept her eyes on the wheel, still trembling, and squeezed his fingers.

qa.q: What was creaking round at the fair?
qa.a: The wooden swing-wheel was creaking round.

qa.q: What was Sudha probably feeling when she said “I want to go” while trembling, and what else could be behind it?
qa.a: A mix of excitement and nerves, since she wanted the ride yet shook her head, then nodded. The cold breeze off the river could also be part of the shaking.

qa.q: What did Tanvir do that suits most possible causes of the shaking?
qa.a: He wrapped the shawl round her and offered to watch one round first, which gives warmth and calm closeness.

qa.q: How might Tanvir see her trembling?
qa.a: He cannot know the cause, so he asks and offers warmth. He may be a little worried she is frightened but does not want to take away her wish to go.

grounding: Trembling may be cold, fear or excitement; warmth and calm closeness address most causes.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage: Bao sat on the edge of the pool in Melbourne, lips pale, knees knocking together. His whole body shook. The lesson had ended with a jump into the deep end, and he had gone last. Lucia, his swimming teacher, wrapped a big towel round his shoulders and sat beside him on the wet tiles. “Cold, or was the jump scary?” Bao's teeth chattered. “Both.” “Want me to rub your back to warm you up?” He nodded, and she rubbed through the towel until the shaking slowed. “You jumped anyway,” she said. He leaned against her arm.

qa.q: What did Lucia wrap round Bao's shoulders?
qa.a: Lucia wrapped a big towel round his shoulders.

qa.q: What might Bao's shaking have meant?
qa.a: It could have been cold from the pool or fear after the deep-end jump; he said both, so he was probably chilly and still a little frightened.

qa.q: Why did Lucia's response work for either cause?
qa.a: A warm towel and calm closeness help with cold and with fear, and she asked Bao, and asked before touching, instead of guessing.

qa.q: How might another child in the class read Bao's shaking?
qa.a: They might think he was only cold, not knowing the jump had scared him too.

grounding: Shows a young child's shaking that could come from cold or fear, and warmth with calm closeness easing both.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage: Backstage at the school's annual day, Asif stood in his paper-crown costume, hands trembling so hard the cardboard rattled. Seema Ma'am knelt in front of him. “Your hands are shaking. Are you scared, or cold, or excited?” Asif bounced on his toes. “Excited! My Abbu is in the third row!” She smiled. “Can I hold them for a moment?” He nodded, and she held his hands, warm between hers. “Big breath with me. In… out.” The shaking eased a little. When the music began, he marched out grinning, crown still wobbling.

qa.q: Where was Asif's Abbu sitting?
qa.a: His Abbu was in the third row.

qa.q: What was Asif feeling as his hands trembled?
qa.a: He felt excited, bouncing on his toes about his Abbu watching; some nerves could be mixed in, since the shaking only eased a little.

qa.q: What did Seema do instead of assuming Asif was afraid?
qa.a: She asked whether it was fear, cold or excitement, then used warm hands and a shared breath, which help whatever the cause.

qa.q: What would change if Seema had told Asif not to be scared?
qa.a: Asif might feel misunderstood, since he was mostly excited, and could start to wonder whether he should be scared.

grounding: Shows a young child trembling from excitement that could be mistaken for fear or cold, and calm, warm closeness settling it.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage: I'm Aditi. Last night my little brother Varun stayed up late building a block tower on the rug. His hands began to shake so much the top blocks kept falling. He wasn't crying, and the room wasn't cold. Mumma picked him up and he flopped onto her shoulder like a sack. “Too tired,” she said, tucking a blanket round him and humming. The shaking stopped once he was asleep. Next morning she told Papa, “If his hands shake like that again when he's rested, we'll ask the doctor.” I don't know what Varun felt. He just looked wobbly.

qa.q: Why did the top blocks keep falling?
qa.a: Varun's hands began to shake so much that the top blocks kept falling.

qa.q: What does Varun flopping onto Mumma's shoulder suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: It suggests he felt worn out and sleepy rather than scared, since he wasn't crying and the room wasn't cold.

qa.q: What plan did Mumma make, and why is it sensible?
qa.a: She will ask the doctor if the shaking comes again when he's rested, because shaking that keeps happening is for a doctor to check.

qa.q: How does Aditi make sense of the shaking?
qa.a: Aditi only sees the falling blocks and the flop onto Mumma's shoulder, and doesn't claim to know what Varun felt.

grounding: Shows a young child's shaking from tiredness, calm closeness settling it, and a plan to see a doctor if it keeps happening.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage:
Sunday: Trisha climbed out of the pool with blue lips, shaking all over. Her papa, Eshaan, wrapped her in the big towel and rubbed her back until the shivers stopped.

Wednesday: Backstage before the school dance, Trisha's hands trembled on her skirt, but she was grinning. Papa held both her hands. "Excited-shaky or scared-shaky?" "Both!"

Saturday: At Chacha's wedding party, near midnight, her legs wobbled and her chin quivered. Papa scooped her onto his lap, and she was asleep in a minute. Later he told Mumma, "Same shivers, three reasons. If it ever kept on with no reason, we'd ask the doctor."

qa.q: What did Papa wrap Trisha in after the pool?
qa.a: The big towel.

qa.q: What was Trisha likely feeling when her hands trembled backstage?
qa.a: Both excited and a little scared, as she says herself; her grin shows the excitement, and the trembling hints at nerves.

qa.q: What helped Trisha each time she shook?
qa.a: Warmth and calm closeness: a towel for the cold, held hands for the nerves and a lap for the tiredness.

qa.q: What would change if the shaking kept going with no clear reason?
qa.a: Then, as Eshaan says, it would be time to ask the doctor rather than only warming or comforting her.

grounding: It shows a young child's trembling coming from cold, excitement and tiredness on different days, eased by warmth and closeness, with a doctor for shaking that keeps on.
